question: Question: Tell me a bio of James B. Donovan.
answer:
James B. Donovan was an American lawyer, diplomatic negotiator, and United States Navy officer who was born on February 29, 1916, and passed away on January 19, 1970. He served in the Office of Scientific Research and Development and the Office of Strategic Services (OSS, predecessor of the Central Intelligence Agency), ultimately becoming general counsel of the OSS.

Donovan is widely known for negotiating the 1960–1962 exchange of captured American U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers for Soviet spy Rudolf Abel, and for negotiating the 1962 release and return of 9,703 prisoners held by Cuba after the failed Bay of Pigs Invasion.

In addition to his diplomatic work, Donovan also had a career in law and publishing. His book "Strangers" (published in 1964 and re-released by Simon & Schuster in August 2015) was widely critically acclaimed and is considered the definitive work on his life and work. He also published a second book, "Challenges: Reflections of a Lawyer-at-Large", in 1967.

Donovan's life and work were the subject of a biography published in 2006, titled "Negotiator: The Life and Career of James B. Donovan" by Philip J. Bigger. Tom Hanks portrayed Donovan in the Coen Brothers film "Bridge of Spies", which was released on October 16, 2015.

In October 2016, Donovan was inducted into the Hall of Honor at Fordham University, where he was also named a founder of the school, in recognition of his accomplishments and contributions. He was also inducted into the All Hallows School Hall of Fame in October 2016. Donovan's family has a connection to Fordham University, as it was founded by Archbishop Hughes, who is an ancestor of Donovan.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Liam Payne.
answer:
Liam Payne is an English singer and songwriter, born on August 29, 1993. He rose to fame as a member of the boy band One Direction, which he joined in 2010 after auditioning for the British television series "The X Factor" twice. The group has since released five albums, embarked on four world tours, and won several awards.

Payne is known as one of the principal songwriters in One Direction, credited for co-writing more than half of the songs on the band's third and fourth album. After leaving One Direction, he began working as a producer under the monikers "Big Payno" or "Payno", teaming up with fellow producers AfterHrs to remix several tracks.

In 2017, Payne made his debut as a solo artist with the release of the single "Strip That Down". He has also collaborated with other artists, such as Rita Ora on the song "For You", which was the lead single from the soundtrack to the film "Fifty Shades Freed".

Payne has been an avid fan of the "Harry Potter" series and has dated singer Cheryl since 2016. They welcomed their first child, a son, on 22 March 2017. Payne and Cheryl announced they had ended their relationship in July 2018.

In 2018, Payne also collaborated with English DJ and record producer Jonas Blue and Canadian singer Lennon Stella on the song "Polaroid". The track was released as a digital download on 5 October 2018 via Virgin EMI Records as the eighth single from Blue's debut studio album "Blue".

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Katsunosuke Hori.
answer:
Katsunosuke Hori, also known as Katsunosuke Matsuoka, was a martial arts master who founded the Shindō Yōshin-ryū, a new system of martial arts that combined his expertise in kenjutsu and jūjutsu. The name Shindō Yōshin-ryū means "new willow school." Katsunosuke intended this new system to embrace a curriculum reflecting that of a "sōgō bujutsu" or integrated martial system, making it militarily applicable.

By 1868, Katsunosuke had witnessed the Meiji Restoration and fought on the losing side of the Boshin War. Following the collapse of the Tokugawa shogunate, Katsunosuke relocated to Ueno Village, north of Edo, where he constructed a new dojo.

In 1895, Katsunosuke authorized another licensed student, Shigeta Ohbata, to separate from the mainline and lead his own branch of Shindō Yōshin-ryū, which became the Ohbata-ha Shindō Yōshin-ryū. Katsunosuke Matsuoka died in 1898 at the age of 62. Without a male heir, the Matsuoka family appointed Matakichi Inose as the temporary headmaster of Shindō Yōshin-ryū.

It's important to note that Katsunosuke Hori is not related to Hori I, Hori II, or any other historical figures named Hori mentioned in the other passages. Katsunosuke Hori is known for his contributions to martial arts, while the other Hori figures are known for their roles in ancient Egyptian history and culture.

Katsu is best known for her debut novel, "The Taker", published in 2011, which was recognized as one of the ten best debut novels of the year by the American Library Association. The novel, a literary work with historical and fantasy elements, has been translated into over a dozen languages. The second novel, "The Reckoning", was nominated for several year-end awards.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Oliver Letwin.
answer:
Oliver Letwin is a British Conservative politician, born on May 19, 1956. He has served as the Member of Parliament for West Dorset since 1997. In 2014, he was appointed as Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, a position he held until 2016. Following the 2015 general election, Letwin was given overall responsibility for the Cabinet Office and became a full member of the Cabinet in the Conservative government.

Prior to his political career, Letwin served as the Minister of State for Government Policy from 2010. He also chaired the Conservative Party's Policy Review from 2005 to 2010 and was the chairman of the Conservative Research Department.

Letwin married Isabel Davidson in 1984, and the couple have two children. He is the son of the Anglo-American academic William Letwin, who played a key role in promulgating the free-market economics of the Thatcher era.

In October 2011, Letwin was involved in a controversy when it was reported that he had thrown away more than 100 secret government documents in public bins. Enquiries made by the Information Commissioner's Office found that although Letwin did not dispose of any government documents, he had in fact disposed of constituents' personal and confidential letters to him and therefore did breach data protection rules. Letwin later apologised for his actions.

In 2016, Letwin was put in charge of the "Brexit unit" after the United Kingdom European Union membership referendum. He maintains the public is willing to increase taxes carefully for large numbers of people to pay for improved public services.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Zamfir Arbore.
answer:
Zamfir Arbore, born Zamfir Ralli on November 14, 1848, was a Bukovinan-born Romanian political activist who spent a significant portion of his life in the Russian Empire. He was also known for his work as an amateur historian, geographer, and ethnographer. Arbore debuted in left-wing politics from an early age, gaining an intimate knowledge of the Russian revolutionary milieu, and participating in both nihilist and Narodnik conspiracies. He became a member of the International Workingmen's Association while self-exiled in Switzerland.

Arbore's revolutionary career was a significant part of his life, although his other commitments, such as his nationalist policies, have been the subject of debate. Some sources claim that his activities in Greater Romania "remain to be investigated."

Arbore returned to Romania at some point but was not allowed entry by the Romanian authorities. He was forced back and later adopted a young child, Zamfir Dumitru Arbore. In 1930, Zamfir Arbore was pensioned from his teaching position at the Bucharest War School, where he had also been lecturing in Geography and Topography.

In later years, Arbore's work was officially quoted and praised in the Soviet Union, despite being on a list of authors officially banned by the Soviet censorship apparatus. In Romania, he was survived by his daughter Nina, known as the Romanian student of Henri Matisse. Nina maintained an interest in moderate leftist causes and joined the group formed around "Cuvântul Liber" newspaper.

Zamfir Arbore's ancestry is a subject of debate among modern researchers. While some see him as descending "from an ancient family of local boyars," others describe him as being tied to the historical Arbores by "a rather thin line." Arbore's "revised past" and arbitrary interpretation of his own background may have been opportunistic, allowing him to gravitate between conflicting national identities and rendering his radical discourse more palatable for all cultural contexts.

Arbore's nephew, Zamfir Dumitru Arbore, fought against Nazi Germany in World War II, receiving "Steaua României."

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Carlos Santana.
answer:
Carlos Santana is a Mexican and American musician, born on July 20, 1947. He is best known for his career as a rock guitarist, particularly as the lead member of the band Santana. The band was formed in 1967 in San Francisco and was originally known as the Carlos Santana Blues Band. The first members included Santana himself, Tom Fraser, Mike Carabello, Rod Harper, David Brown, and Gregg Rolie.

Santana's discography consists of 24 studio albums, seven live albums, 61 singles, and 23 compilation albums. His breakthrough began in 1969, playing at the Woodstock Festival. Over the years, lineup changes were common and frequent in the band.

Santana has also collaborated on numerous albums with various artists, such as Chad Kroeger and Steven Tyler, and appeared in forty-nine albums as a guest guitarist. He has received a certification for only two of his prior released albums, his debut album "Love Devotion Surrender", and the live album "Carlos Santana & Buddy Miles! Live!".

In 1994, he collaborated with his brother Jorge Santana and his nephew Carlos Hernandez on an album called "Santana Brothers". He has been married twice, first to Deborah Santana for 34 years, and later to drummer Cindy Blackman, whom he proposed to during a concert in 2010. They live in Las Vegas.

Santana has had significant success with the albums "Shaman" (which included two number one singles, "Smooth" and "Maria Maria") and "Supernatural". He has been recognized for his guitar skills, being named number fifteen on "Rolling Stone"'s list of the 100 Greatest Guitarists of All Time in 2003. In 2013, he was honored as a Kennedy Center Honoree. On November 4, 2014, his memoir, "The Universal Tone: Bringing My Story to Light" was published.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Julia Faye.
answer:
Julia Faye (born Julia Faye Maloney, September 24, 1892 – April 6, 1966) was an American actress known for her appearances in more than 30 productions by Cecil B. DeMille, a prominent filmmaker of the silent and sound film eras. She was born near Richmond, Virginia, and her father worked for the Atchison, Topeka, and Santa Fe Railway.

Faye started her acting career in 1914, appearing in several Keystone comedies and a minor role in D. W. Griffith's "Intolerance" (1916). Her first role for Cecil B. DeMille was in "The Woman God Forgot" (1917). She continued working for DeMille in various productions, including "The Whispering Chorus" and "The Volga Boatman" (1926), which established her as "one of Hollywood's popular leading ladies."

Faye was famed throughout Hollywood for her perfect legs until her performance in "The Volga Boatman." She married Harold Leroy Wallick in 1913, but he predeceased her. In 1917, she met Cecil B. DeMille and became one of his mistresses. Faye later married screenwriter Walter Anthony Merrill.

Faye's career continued through the 1920s and 1930s, with notable roles in films such as "Old Wives for New," "The Squaw Man," and "Till I Come Back to You" (all 1918), "Stepping Out" (1919), and "Male and Female" (1919). Her last role was as a dowager in the 1958 remake of DeMille's "The Buccaneer," produced by DeMille himself but directed by his son-in-law Anthony Quinn.

Her memoir, saved in The Cecil B. DeMille Archives at Brigham Young University, has yet to be published. Faye was awarded a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame at 6500 Hollywood Boulevard.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Toru Muranishi.
answer:
Toru Muranishi, also known as Toro Muranishi, was born in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan in 1948. After graduating from high school, he moved to Tokyo where he sold encyclopedias. He subsequently became involved in book publishing and the entertainment industry. In late 1984, Muranishi joined the newly formed AV studio Crystal-Eizou and began directing films with them soon afterwards.

Muranishi is credited for launching the career of one of the first AV superstars, Kaoru Kuroki, who made her debut at Crystal-Eizou in October 1986. Among his pioneering developments at Crystal-Eizou were his series which culminated in a facial, and a series which satirized contemporary food-oriented practices.

Muranishi is also a prolific writer, contributing to blogs on Japanese AV supplier DMM's website and his own website, as well as a series of articles going back to 2005 at policejapan.com. He has published a number of books, including "Toru Muranishi's Grade Book" and "The Sex Shogun of Shinjuku", a British Channel 4 TV documentary that explored his career and the documentary porn genre.

Throughout his career, Muranishi has had numerous problems with the law, having been convicted seven times of criminal violations. In June 1986, he was arrested for violating the Japanese law by using an underage actress in videos. He also faced legal issues during a "legendary session" where he filmed 30 videos in 30 days in Hawaii, flying in 15 or so actresses in turn from Japan for the shoot.

As an actor, Muranishi appeared in the 2000 Soft On Demand (SOD) produced V-Cinema "Renshin Joshikousei Patty". He is the subject of various documentaries, including "It Is Nice", which won a special award at the New Directors Film Festival in Tokyo in November 2014.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Gonzalo Fonseca.
answer:
Gonzalo Fonseca was a Uruguayan artist known for his stone sculpting, born on July 2, 1922, in Montevideo, Uruguay. He originally studied to be an architect at the University of Montevideo, but discovered modern art in 1942 after working in the Taller Torres-Garcia workshop. He studied painting in the workshop until 1949, and became interested in pre-Columbian art during that time. Fonseca is frequently associated with the movement Universal Constructivism.

In the 1930s, Fonseca traveled to Europe, where he was exposed to archaeology, anthropology, and history. He continued his artistic journey, and his works are now recognized globally. Fonseca passed away on June 11, 1997.

Notable works by Fonseca include the "Tower of the Winds", built in 1974 as a tribute. He had studios in the East Village of Manhattan and in Pietrasanta in Tuscany.

Fonseca was the father of Caio Fonseca, an American painter, and Isabel Fonseca, an American-Uruguayan writer. Bruno Fonseca, another painter, was his brother, and Quina Fonseca, a designer, was also among his siblings.

His first album, "The Nebulizer", was released on 14 October 2011, produced by Nebs.

Kerser gained fame with the track "Kerser is the sickest" from his first album. His second album, "No Rest for the Sickest", was released on 2 November 2012, reaching No. 15 on the ARIA Albums Chart and No. 1 on the ARIA Urban Albums Chart. Kerser's fifth album titled "Next Step" was released on 13 November 2015, produced by Sinima Beats. It was his first album to be released under his label ABK Records and was distributed by Warner Music Australia. 1. Prince Regent River (Western Australia):
The Prince Regent River is a river in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. Its headwaters rise in the Caroline Range near Mount Agnes and flow in a north-westerly direction. The river runs a uniquely straight course following a fault line for the majority of its length. It enters and flows through the Prince Regent National Park, past King Cascade, and discharges into Saint George Basin and Hanover Bay, eventually reaching the Indian Ocean. The river has six tributaries, including Quail Creek, Youwanjela Creek, Womarama Creek, and Pitta Creek. The river was visited by surveyor Frederick Brockman in 1901. The traditional owners of the area are the Worora peoples, and eighteen freshwater fish species are known to inhabit the waters of the Prince Regent River.

2. Hunter River (Prince Edward Island):
The Hunter River, informally known as the "River Clyde," is a Canadian river in northwestern Queens County, Prince Edward Island. From its source near Hartsville, the river flows northerly, becoming a tidal estuary at New Glasgow, an arm of Rustico Bay. It discharges into the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The river's total meander length is about 100 km, with an additional 20 km of estuary. The river runs through the communities of Hunter River, New Glasgow, and North Rustico. There was at one time a ferry at Hunter River. The original community name was Dog River (changed to Clyde River sometime around 1864). It was named after the River Clyde in Scotland. The heritage of the area is predominantly Scottish and English.

It was initially reported that she would have a romantic track with N. T. Rama Rao Jr. in "Rabhasa," but this was later found to be false. In "Durga" (2014), she was initially cast, but she was later replaced by Hansika Motwani.

Samantha has also worked in Tamil films, including "Vinnaithaandi Varuvaayaa" (2010), "Thanga Magan" (2015), and "Theri" (2016). She has won several awards for her performances, including three Filmfare Awards South.

Apart from acting, Samantha is also known for her philanthropic work and has been involved in various social causes. She is married to actor Naga Chaitanya.

Kim Casali (September 9, 1941 – June 15, 1997) was a New Zealand cartoonist who created the syndicated cartoon feature "Love Is..." in the late 1960s. She was born Marilyn Judith Grove in Auckland, New Zealand, and left home at the age of 19 to travel around Australia, Europe, and the United States. In 1967, she moved to Los Angeles where she met and began a relationship with Roberto Alfredo Vincenzo Casali, an Italian computer engineer.

Casali had been drawing cartoons of humorous incidents, such as those she observed on the ski slopes, and Roberto encouraged her to continue. The couple's relationship and Casali's cartoons eventually led to the creation of the "Love Is..." cartoon feature, which was originally intended as love notes to her future husband.

In one of the first cases of its kind, Casali gave birth to a child sixteen months after the death of her husband, having been artificially inseminated using his stored frozen sperm. This case, which predated the Warnock Report, gave rise to legal discussions regarding the baby's rights of inheritance and made front-page news across the world. The birth split public opinion, with some applauding Casali's bravery and others, including the Vatican newspaper "L'Osservatore Romano," disagreeing with her actions.

After the birth of her child, Casali received hundreds of letters applauding her bravery. In the mid-1980s, she moved the family to New South Wales, Australia, and bought a farm north of Sydney where she bred Arabian horses for several years. In 1990, she returned to England and settled in Leatherhead, Surrey.

Casali died due to cancer of the bone and liver in 1997. In 1996, she gave a rare interview in which she deplored the courts' involvement in a similar case involving a widow seeking impregnation with her husband's sperm, stating that such matters should be dealt with privately.

Born on December 27, 1985, Rami began his football career playing for amateur club Étoile Fréjus Saint-Raphaël, then known as ES Fréjus. He spent three seasons at the club playing in the Championnat de France amateur, the fourth division of French football.

In 2006, Rami ascended three divisions after signing with Ligue 1 club Lille. At Lille, Rami developed into a starter, making his professional debut in May 2007. He is nicknamed "the lion of Fréjus."

In the 2007–08 season, Rami was declared a starter by Puel and inserted at centre-back, alongside captain Grégory Tafforeau. In the opening match of the season, against Lorient, Rami featured in the match until the 69th minute, when he suffered an injury to ligaments in one of his ankles.

Rami received his first call-up to the France national team in 2008 by then head coach Raymond Domenech for a friendly match against England. He has stated on several occasions that he would prefer to "represent Morocco within the France team."

Rami is a Muslim and was dating Canadian actress Pamela Anderson in 2017, and as of November 2018, the two were living together in the French Riviera. He signed his first professional contract in 2008, agreeing to a three-year deal lasting until 2010. He was then promoted to the senior squad on a permanent basis and assigned the number 23 shirt.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Wahida Prism Khan.
answer:
Wahida Prism Khan is an Indian naval surgeon, born in 1972 in Thanamandi, Rajouri. She was the first woman from Jammu & Kashmir to join the Indian Navy and the first woman in India to command the annual parade at the Armed Forces Medical College, Pune in 2006.

Khan was born to Gulzar Ahmed and Hajara Kaser, who were teachers by profession. She is one of five siblings, with her elder sister Jubin serving as Deputy Superintendent in J&K Police. Tragedy struck when Khan's father was killed while at work in the school where he was the head master. The school was attacked.

Khan completed her schooling at Thanamandi in Rajouri, her intermediate from the Government Girls School Rajouri, and her MBBS from Government Medical College, Jammu. She developed an interest in unconventional activities such as riding a motorcycle and climbing mountains as a young girl, which was not usual in her society. This led to her family having to leave the town.

Khan joined the Armed Forces Medical College to fulfill her father's desire of serving in the armed forces. In 1997, she took an orientation training course at the Officer's Training School at Lucknow and was then commissioned in the Navy in 1997. She has served the Indian Navy as the Surgeon Captain and has served aboard naval ship INS Amba for 19 months. She is now aiming to become the first woman to work in submarines.

In 2005, Khan's doctors suspected a malignant growth but she later recovered. In 2007, the National Council of Education Research and Trainings (NCERT) incorporated her story in a special chapter for Class IV students. In 2016, she was appointed as Additional Ship Safety Officer (ASSO) at Naval Ship Angre under Head Quarter Western Naval Command.

Khan married Major M. F. Khan, a pathologist by profession and former Short Service Commissioned (SSC) Officer. She attributes her success to her husband.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Abdou Diallo.
answer:
Abdou Diallo is a French professional footballer who was born on May 4, 1996, in Tours, France. He joined the youth academy of AS Monaco FC at the age of 15 and signed his first professional contract with the club on March 28, 2014. Vadim Vasilyev, the vice-president of AS Monaco, commented that Diallo "fits perfectly into our sports project. He has a lot of talent and we hope that he will continue to progress alongside the great players of AS Monaco".

Diallo plays as a defender for Borussia Dortmund. He joined Borussia Dortmund in 2018 and scored his first goal for the club in a 3–1 league victory against Eintracht Frankfurt on September 15, 2018. Rouven Schröder, the sporting director of 1. FSV Mainz, has described Diallo as "strong in the air and shrewd in the challenge". Michael Zorc, the sporting director of Borussia Dortmund, described Diallo as "a modern, strong central defender who is very intelligent. He can play a variety of defensive roles, including as a central defender and even in a defensive midfield role".

Diallo is of Senegalese descent and is the older brother of the footballer Ibrahima Diallo, who plays as a midfielder for the French club Stade Brestois 29 in the Ligue 2, on loan from Monaco. Diallo also captains France's U-21 Team.

It is worth noting that there is also an Abdou Moumouni University in Niamey, Niger, named after a Nigerien educator, intellectual, and president of the university. However, it is unclear if there is any connection between this university and the footballer Abdou Diallo.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Kalki Koechlin.

Kalki Koechlin is a French actress and writer, born on 10 January 1984 in Pondicherry, India, to French parents. She grew up with an interest in theatre and studied drama at Goldsmiths, University of London. Koechlin is known for her unconventional body of work in the Hindi film industry and has received accolades such as a National Film Award, a Filmfare, and two Screen Awards. She was also conferred with the Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters by the French Minister of Culture for her contributions to cinema.

Koechlin has worked in various films, including "Dev.D", "Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara", "Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani", and "Margarita with a Straw". She has also been a part of web-series like "Fault", "Printing Machine", and "Man's World". Outside film, Koechlin has written, produced, and acted in several stage plays. She co-wrote the drama "Skeleton Woman" and made her directorial debut on stage with the tragicomedy "Living Room". Koechlin has also hosted a travel show entitled "Kalki's Great Escape".

In addition to her acting career, Koechlin is an activist and promotes various causes ranging from health and education to women's empowerment and gender equality. She has been the brand ambassador of the "Cinema For Care" section aimed at creating awareness about disability issues at the All Lights India International Film Festival.

André Koechlin, who is an ancestor of Kalki Koechlin, was a French industrialist and the railroad equipment maker from the Koechlin family. He was born in France to the Koechlin family, where he was the grandson of Samuel Koechlin, son-in-law of Daniel Dollfus-Mieg, head of the Dollfus-Mieg textile company. Under his lead, between 1818 and 1826, the company became the leading textile company of Mulhouse. Turning in 1826 to the building of machinery for the textile industry, Koechlin became knowledgeable in the fabrication of various machines.

He was one of the most notorious and dangerous gangsters in Malaysia during the 1960s and 1970s. He was known for conducting armed robberies, and was often regarded as a modern-day Robin Hood, as some say he shared the cash from the robberies with the poor.

On the evening of February 16, Botak Chin reportedly received income from a robbery and "reinvested in his business" by going to Thailand to buy more firearms and ammunition. The gang used a vacant tin mine in Kepong as their shooting range, using stray dogs for target practice.

Despite his criminal activities, Botak Chin had a desire to help the poor and downtrodden, and wanted to protect them from corrupt officials and gangsters who extorted money from them.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Chris Cheney.
answer:
Chris Cheney is an Australian rock musician, record producer, and studio owner, born on January 2, 1975. He is the founding mainstay guitarist, songwriter, and lead vocalist of the psychobilly band, The Living End, which he formed in 1994 with school mate Scott Owen. The Living End is known for their top 20 hits on the ARIA Singles Chart, including "Second Solution" / "Prisoner of Society" (1997), "All Torn Down" (1999), "Pictures in the Mirror" (2000), "Roll On" (2001), "One Said to the Other" (2003), "What's on Your Radio" (2005), "Wake Up" (2006), and "White Noise" (2008).

In addition to his work with The Living End, Cheney has also collaborated with other artists. In October 2011, he released an EP, "The Bright and Blue," and was a guest on "RocKwiz" for a second time, performing with US-born rocker, Suzi Quatro. In 2017, he filled in for Chris Shiflett on the spring tour of "Me First and the Gimme Gimmes."

Cheney is known for playing a Gretsch White Falcon guitar and using mainly distortion and modulation effects. He has his own signature series Gretsch guitars and is endorsed by Gretsch Guitars.

Before forming The Living End, Cheney played in other bands, including Goodbye Sideburns Forever and The Runaway Boys, where he played guitar alongside Scott Owen on piano and double bass.

Burrell began her career performing with Reverend James Cleveland's GMWA Youth Mass Choir, Trinity Temple Full Gospel Mass Choir of Dallas, and The Inspirational Sounds Mass Choir of Houston. In 1996, she was a featured singer on the reprise of "Jesus Paid It All" on Ricky Dillard & New G's album "Worked It Out".

In 2010, Burrell founded The Love & Liberty Fellowship Pentecostal Overcoming Holy Church, where she serves as Senior Eldress/Overseer-Bishop. She is divorced and has a son, Christian. In December 2016, a video surfaced showing Burrell preaching a sermon at the Love & Liberty Fellowship Church, where she called people who engage in homosexual acts "perverted" and said they had been deceived by the "homosexual spirit." She also warned that people who "play with" homosexual sin would "die from it."

In response to the criticism, Burrell said that she makes "no excuses or apologies" for the sermon, adding "I love you, and God loves you, but he hates the sin in you and me." This led to the cancellation of her scheduled appearance on "The Ellen DeGeneres Show" and the BMI Trailblazers of Gospel Music event, where she was removed as an honoree.

Despite the controversy, Burrell continued her career and released her newest album "Kim Burrell Live in Miami" in 2017. She also collaborated with Pharrell Williams for the soundtrack to the feature film "Hidden Figures" in 2016. In 2018, she brought her Church Love & Liberty under the organization from Dr Kevin Williams New Jerusalem Cathedral Greensboro North Carolina.

Moynahan is best known for her role in the police drama "Blue Bloods," where she plays Assistant District Attorney Erin Reagan. She moved from Pacific Palisades, California to New York when she was cast in this role in 2010. She has also starred in films such as "Noise" (2007), "Ramona and Beezus" (2010), and "I, Frankenstein" (2011).

In addition to her acting career, Moynahan has also worked as a spokesmodel for Garnier, promoting their skincare products. She lived with screenwriter Scott Rosenberg from 2004 to 2006. In 2010, she moved to New York and began dating director McG. On October 17, 2015, she married businessman Andrew Frankel at a ceremony in the Hamptons. Moynahan has a son from a previous relationship.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Maneka Gandhi.
answer:
Maneka Gandhi, born on August 26, 1956, is the Indian Union Cabinet Minister for Women & Child Development in the Government of PM Narendra Modi. She is also an animal rights activist, environmentalist, and the widow of the Indian politician Sanjay Gandhi. Maneka was born in Delhi into a Sikh family, her father being Lt. Col. Tarlochan Singh, an Indian Army officer. She studied at Lawrence School and later at Lady Shri Ram College for Women, and subsequently studied German at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi.

Maneka first met Sanjay Gandhi at a cocktail party in 1973 and married him in 1974. During the Emergency, Sanjay Gandhi rose in politics, and Maneka was often seen with him on his tours, helping with his work. After a fallout with Indira Gandhi, Maneka moved out of the prime minister's residence.

Maneka founded the Rashtriya Sanjay Manch along with Akbar Ahmed Dumpy, a party primarily focused on youth empowerment and employment. It won four out of five seats in the Elections in Andhra Pradesh. She published 'The Complete Book of Muslim and Parsi Names', in recognition of her husband's Zoroastrian faith, and later published 'The Book of Hindu Names' (Penguin).

Maneka contested the Amethi constituency from Uttar Pradesh for the 1984 general election for the Loksabha but lost to Rajiv Gandhi. In 1988, she joined V.P. Singh's Janata Dal and campaigned with him. Maneka Gandhi has been a minister in four governments and has authored a number of books in the areas of etymology, law, and animal welfare.

In recent years, Maneka Gandhi has made headlines for her comments on suicide rates and hormonal outbursts in young women. She has also been involved in advocating for animal rights and environmental conservation.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Bella Akhmadulina.
answer:
Bella Akhmadulina was a renowned Soviet and Russian poet, short story writer, and translator, born on April 10, 1937, in Moscow. She was the only child of a Tatar father and a Russian-Italian mother, and her family underwent evacuation to Kazan during World War II.

Akhmadulina's literary career began at a young age when she worked as a journalist at the Moscow newspaper, "Metrostroevets", and honed her poetic skills at a circle organized by the poet Yevgeny Vinokurov. Her first poems were published in 1955 in the magazine "October" after being approved by established Soviet poets.

Known for her apolitical writing stance, Akhmadulina was part of the Russian New Wave literary movement. Despite this, she was critical of authorities in the Soviet Union and spoke out in favor of Nobel laureates such as Boris Pasternak, Andrei Sakharov, and others.

Akhmadulina was recognized as one of the Soviet Union's literary treasures and a classic poet in the long line extending from Lermontov and Pushkin. She was known internationally via her travels abroad during the Khrushchev Thaw, during which she made appearances in sold-out stadiums.

Her main themes were friendship, love, and relations between people. She wrote numerous essays about Russian poets and translators, some devoted to her close friend, Bulat Okudzhava. Akhmadulina avoided writing overtly political poems but took part in political events in her youth, supporting the so-called "dissident movement".

She translated poetry from various countries including France, Italy, Chechnya, Poland, Yugoslavia, Hungary, Bulgaria, Georgia, Armenia, and many others. Akhmadulina wrote in a "resolutely apolitical" style, using imagery and humor in her work. She made use of rhymed quatrains in her early works, which discussed ordinary, yet imaginative occurrences from everyday life.

Akhmadulina died at her home in Peredelkino near Moscow on November 29, 2010, at the age of 73, due to a heart condition

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Anna May Wong.
answer:
Anna May Wong was an American actress, born on January 3, 1905, in Los Angeles. She was of Hong Kong-Chinese descent, making her the first Hong Kong-Chinese American Hollywood movie star and the first Chinese American actress to gain international recognition. Her career spanned various mediums, including silent films, sound films, television, stage, and radio.

Wong developed a passion for acting at a young age and began her film career early. During the silent film era, she acted in "The Toll of the Sea" (1922), one of the first films to feature an Asian lead.

Throughout her career, Wong faced racial discrimination and stereotyping in the roles she was offered. However, she refused to play the Chinese character in one of her films, instead using her knowledge of Chinese style and gestures to add authenticity to the character.

Following her return to Hollywood in 1930, Wong turned to the stage and cabaret for creative outlets. Tragedy struck in 1930 when her mother was killed by an automobile. Wong continued to support her younger siblings' education.

Wong's life, career, and legacy have been the subject of various biographies and literary works. Her career is often portrayed as one of "tragic glamour" and she is remembered as a pioneer in Asian-American cinematic history.

Anthony Chan, in his work, highlights Wong's place in Asian-American cinematic history as its first female star. Other notable works about Wong include "Anna May Wong: A Complete Guide to Her Film, Stage, Radio and Television Work" by Philip Leibfried and Chei Mi Lane, and "Anna May Wong: From Laundryman's Daughter to Hollywood Legend" by Graham Russell Hodges.

Anna May Wong passed away on February 3, 1961. Despite her death, her impact on the entertainment industry and Asian-American representation continues to be felt.

Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, poet, and travel writer, best known for his works "Treasure Island," "Kidnapped," and "Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde."

In 1880, Stevenson, along with his new wife Fanny Vandegrift Osbourne, spent their honeymoon living in a cabin at a played-out mine on Mount Saint Helena in California, which is now named after him as Robert Louis Stevenson State Park.

In 1888, Stevenson was granted temporary residence on Abemama, an island in the Pacific, by the local chief, Tembinok'. This stay was immortalized by Stevenson's description of Tembinok' in his book "In the South Seas."

Stevenson spent two months on Abemama in 1889. Later, he moved to Samoa, where he lived until his death in 1894. His connection with Samoa continued even after his death, as his school, Robert Louis Stevenson School, was established in Samoa's capital city of Apia. The school, which is based on an Australian and New Zealand curricula, is known for educating children from Samoa's richest families and for having a school roll with mainly "afakasi" (mixed) pupils.

Stevenson's works have had a significant impact on literature, and he is remembered as one of the great authors of the late 19th century. His works continue to be popular and widely read today.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Egon Krenz.
answer:
Egon Krenz was born on March 19, 1937, and served as the last communist leader of East Germany during the final months of 1989. He succeeded Erich Honecker as the General Secretary of the Socialist Unity Party of Germany (SED), but was forced to resign only months later when the Berlin Wall fell. Throughout his career, Krenz held a number of prominent positions in the SED, serving as Honecker's deputy from 1984 onward.

Krenz was commander-in-chief of the National People's Army, and his appointment as leader was not unanimous, with some deputies voting against and abstaining. In his first address as leader, Krenz promised democratic reforms, but few East Germans believed him. Krenz was almost as detested as Honecker had been, and one popular joke compared him to Honecker.

Despite promises of reform, public opposition to the regime continued to grow. Krenz was forced to send Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski to beg West Germany for a short-term loan to make interest payments, but West Germany was unwilling to negotiate until the SED abandoned power and allowed free elections. Krenz was unwilling to concede to this demand.

Krenz was also personally involved in rejecting the application of the dissident group New Forum to become an approved organization. After serving nearly four years of his sentence, Krenz was released from prison in December 2003 and retired to Dierhagen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Unlike other high-ranking former members of the SED, Krenz still defends the old East Germany and maintains he has not changed his political views.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Alexandre Guilmant.
answer:
Alexandre Guilmant was a French organist, composer, pedagogue, performer, and improviser, born on March 12, 1837, in Meudon. He received his initial musical education from his father and later studied under the Belgian master Jacques-Nicolas Lemmens.

Guilmant served as the organist at La Trinité church from 1871 until 1901. During this time, he also helped found the Schola Cantorum de Paris and was appointed as Professor of Organ at the Paris Conservatoire in 1896.

Guilmant was a prolific composer, with a focus on works for the organ, his own instrument. Some of his notable compositions include 'Pièces dans différents styles', 'L'organiste pratique', Eighteen 'Pièces Nouvelles', and 'L'Organiste liturgique'. His Eight Sonatas were specifically conceived with the Cavaillé-Coll organ of La Trinité in mind.

Guilmant was also a significant figure in the musical education of several notable organists, including Marcel Dupré, whom he began teaching at the age of 11. Guilmant championed Dupré's career and did much to advance his success.

In addition to his original compositions, Guilmant, along with his younger colleague André Pirro, published a collection of scores, "Archives des Maîtres de l'Orgue" (Archives of the Masters of the Organ), which compiled the compositions of numerous pre-1750 French composers. He also published "l'École classique de l'Orgue" (Classical School of the Organ), a survey of organ pieces by foreign composers.

Guilmant passed away on March 29, 1911. His contributions to the organ repertoire and his influence on the next generation of organists continue to be felt today.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Marie Alexandrine Becker.
answer:
Marie Alexandrine Becker, also known as "The Black Widow," was a Belgian serial killer born on July 14, 1877, in the rural village of Wamont near Landen. She was raised in a peasant environment and rarely attended school to help her parents in the fields.

In 1905, she met her future husband, Charles Becker, Sr., at the Universal Exhibition in Liège. She climbed the social ladder, transitioning from a saleswoman to managing the fittings in a large fashion store on Pot d'Or Street in Liège. She married Charles Becker Sr. and they moved into a house adjoined to the family sawmill, where Mr. Becker and his two sons, Charles Jr. and Gustave, worked.

However, Marie did not get along well with the family, particularly Gustave's wife, Léontine. In 1912, Charles Becker Jr. died from cancer. Marie used some of the acquired money to pay off debts and maintain her lover, Maximilien Houdy, who was twenty years younger.

In 1933, she relaunched a seamstress day business for wealthy clients and began to take care of court ladies, as suggested by a friend. Between 1933 and 1936, she was sentenced to death for poisoning eleven people and attempting to poison five others. However, since capital punishment in Belgium had not been applied since 1863, her sentence was commuted to life imprisonment. Marie Alexandrine Becker died in the Forest Prison during the Second World War on June 11, 1942.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Luis N. Rivera-Pagán.
answer:
Luis N. Rivera-Pagán is the Henry Winters Luce Professor Emeritus of Ecumenics at Princeton Theological Seminary. He was born on December 5, 1942, in San Juan de Puerto Rico, Puerto Rico. Rivera-Pagán earned his M. Div. at the Evangelical Seminary of Puerto Rico in 1966, S.T.M. (1967) and M.A. (1968) at Yale University, and in 1970, he received his PhD from Yale with the dissertation "Unity and Truth: The Unity of God, Man, Jesus Christ, and the Church in Irenaeus", under Jaroslav Pelikan.

Between 1970 and 2003, Rivera-Pagán was a Professor of Systematic theology at the Evangelical Seminary of Puerto Rico and Professor of Humanities at the University of Puerto Rico. In 1999, he was the John Alexander Mackay Visiting Professor on World Christianity at Princeton Theological Seminary, which led to his appointment in 2003 to the faculty of Princeton Theological Seminary as the Henry Winters Luce Professor of Ecumenics and Mission. He retired in June 2007 with the status of Professor-emeritus.

Rivera-Pagán spent the academic year of 1969-1970 studying at the University of Tübingen, Germany. Between 1970 and 2003, he was also a chair of Humanities at the Faculty of General Studies of the University of Puerto Rico.

Rivera-Pagán is a prolific author, who wrote, co-authored, edited, and co-edited dozens of books, journal issues, chapters, articles, and reviews in books and journals. He is known for his work in the field of ecumenics and systematic theology.

Her brother, Robert Sedgwick, is also an actor. He made his debut on the television soap opera "Another World" as Hunter Bradshaw in 1984. Sedgwick herself graduated from Bennington College in 1984.

In 2005, Sedgwick appeared in the film "Loverboy" alongside her brother-in-law Kevin Bacon, with whom she is married, and their children, Travis and Sosie.

Theodore Sedgwick, who is the fourth great-grandfather of actress Kyra Sedgwick, was a prominent figure in American history. He was a lawyer, politician, and a member of the United States House of Representatives. He served as Speaker of the House from 1789 to 1793.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Andrew Shue.
answer:
Andrew Shue is an American actor, entrepreneur, and philanthropist, born on February 20, 1967, in Wilmington, Delaware. He is best known for his role as Billy Campbell on the television series "Melrose Place" from 1992 to 1999.

Shue served on the Board of Directors for Do Something, a non-profit organization he co-founded, and is also the co-founder of the social networking website CafeMom. His father, James W. Shue, was a lawyer and real estate developer, and his mother, Anne Brewster Shue, was a bank executive.

Shue has a younger brother, Elisabeth Shue, who is also an actress. He has two half-siblings from his father's remarriage, Jenna and Harvey Shue. Shue graduated from Columbia High School in Maplewood, New Jersey, where he and Elisabeth were inducted into the school's Hall of Fame in 1994.

In addition to acting, Shue has ventured into business. He co-founded CafeMom, an online community for moms to connect and share advice and ideas. The site's community forums were shut down in May 2018 due to high advertising costs. CafeMom is now a family of companies, including blog The Stir, Baby Name Wizard, and popular Latina site MamasLatinas.

Currently, Shue co-hosts the webisode series "Mad Life" along with comedian Chuck Nice and his mother-in-law Joanie Robach (mother of Amy Robach). Shue is also involved in various philanthropic activities and serves on the board of several non-profit organizations.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Mauro Icardi.
answer:
Mauro Icardi is an Argentine professional footballer who currently plays as a striker for Italian club Inter Milan, serving as the team's captain, and the Argentina national team. Born on February 19, 1993, Icardi is a prolific goal scorer and has been described as "an animal in the box" and a "deadly striker".

Icardi began his professional career at Sampdoria after being in Barcelona's youth system La Masia. He joined Inter Milan in July 2013 and has since scored over 100 goals in Serie A for them, making him Inter's ninth highest goalscorer of all time. Icardi won the "Capocannoniere" (the top scorer in Serie A) in 2014–15 and 2017–18, being the joint winner in both seasons. He was named the new captain of Inter after the 2014–15 season.

Icardi has been a subject of controversy due to his marriage to Wanda Nara, whose ex-husband is Icardi's former Sampdoria teammate Maxi López. López and Nara divorced because of her exposed relationship with Icardi. Icardi is of Italian origin through his paternal ancestors named Icardi from Piedmont and Da Mezan from Venice. He has an Italian passport.

Icardi was also the cover of the Italian version of EA Sports' "FIFA 16", alongside global cover star and compatriot Lionel Messi. He has been integral for Inter reaching a place in the UEFA Champions League, which was their first time in six years. Icardi joined Barcelona at the start of the 2008–09 season and was included on the U-17 team. He later joined Sampdoria on loan in January 2011. Icardi later stated that leaving Barcelona was not a bad decision, convinced that his decision to move on was the right one.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Ram Gopal Varma.
answer:
Ram Gopal Varma is an Indian film director, screenwriter, and producer, known for his works in Telugu cinema, Bollywood, and television. He is regarded as one of the pioneers of new age Indian cinema. Varma has directed films across multiple genres, including parallel cinema and docudrama, noted for their gritty realism, technical finesse, and craft.

He garnered the National Film Award for scripting the political crime drama, "Shool" (1999). In 2004, he was featured in the BBC World series "Bollywood Bosses". In his career, he has won several awards such as the National Film Award, the Bimal Roy Memorial National Award, seven state Nandi Awards, two Bollywood Filmfare Awards, and five Bollywood Movie Awards.

Ram Gopal Varma is also known for arranging special screenings of his films. For instance, he arranged a special screening of "The Attacks of 26/11" for Senior officials and journalists.

He introduced several actors and directors to the industry, including Uttej, Ravi Teja, and Bramhaji. Uttej was introduced by Ram Gopal Varma with the Telugu film "Siva" in 1989 and won the Nandi Award for the film Chandamama as a comedian.

In addition to his work in films, Ram Gopal Varma has also been appreciated for his good deeds in the film industry. He completed his schooling at Jangaon, Warangal, and has two daughters named Chetana who is a child artist and acted in Teja's "Chitram" and Pata.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Shashank Manohar.
answer:
Shashank Vyankatesh Manohar is a prominent Indian lawyer and cricket administrator, born on September 29, 1957. He comes from a well-known family of lawyers. His maternal uncle, Justice M.L Pendse, was a legendary Judge of the Bombay High Court. His younger brother, Sunil Manohar, served as the Advocate General of Maharashtra, and his sister, Vasanti Naik, is a Judge at the Bombay High Court.

Shashank Manohar is a Chitpavan Brahman and his mother tongue is Marathi. He is equally fluent in Hindi and English. He is known to be an introvert bordering on the recluse, but rarely loses his cool. When he does, he grows quieter.

Manohar served as the President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) twice, first from 2008 to 2011, and then from November 2015 to May 2016. He also served as the chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) from November 2015 to March 2017. On March 24, 2017, a resolution was passed to reinstate him as the chairman until a successor was elected.

During his presidency, India became the No. 1 Test side and won the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup, defeating Sri Lanka. He is credited for bringing transparency to the activities of the BCCI, developing the bench strength of the Indian team, reinvigorating Women's cricket, and starting the National Cricket Academy (NCA) again.

In 1979, Shashank Manohar married Varsha Oka. Their son, Adwait Manohar, is a lawyer in Nagpur and currently a Vice-President of Vidarbha Cricket Association.

Neumann is a Christian and has been described as part of the Labor Right. He was initially opposed to same-sex marriage but changed his position in December 2015. He has been against pushes to repeal Section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act.

In the Australian Labor Party leadership spill on 26 June 2013, Neumann supported Kevin Rudd. He is from Queensland.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Siti Rahmah Kassim.
answer:
Siti Rahmah Kassim was an independence fighter from Malaysia, born on November 30, 1926, and passed away on March 24, 2017. She is best known for donating her golden bangle to Tunku Abdul Rahman, Malaysia's first Prime Minister, to help fund his travel to London for negotiations of Malaysia's independence from the United Kingdom.

Siti Rahmah began her political career at the young age of 18, actively protesting against the Malayan Union. In 1959, she became the first woman to contest in the general election, holding the Tementang seat in Rembau for two consecutive terms on the Alliance ticket until 1969.

Throughout her life, Siti Rahmah held various posts, including the chairman of the Negri Sembilan Islamic Welfare Organisation of Malaysia (Perkim), deputy president of the Negri Sembilan Single Mothers' Association and Malaysian Single Mothers Council, and head of the Rembau Kaum Ibu association for 17 years.

In her later years, Siti Rahmah remained active in UMNO, expressing her commitment to the party and urging against party hopping. She passed away in Kelana Jaya, Petaling Jaya, and her body was brought to the Al-Hidayah Mosque for funeral prayers before being buried. Her contribution to Malaysia's independence and her political career will be remembered as significant.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Fran Unsworth.
answer:
Fran Unsworth is a British journalist and media executive, born on December 29, 1957, in Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire. She attended St Dominic's High School for Girls, an independent grammar school in Stoke-on-Trent, and studied drama at the University of Manchester.

Unsworth began her broadcasting career in local radio, working at BBC Radio Leicester and BBC Radio Bristol. She then moved to Radio 1 and became Producer of "Newsbeat." In 1990, she moved to Radio 4 and was based in Washington as a radio producer during the Gulf crisis of 1990–1991. She worked as a producer on "The World at One" and "PM" while at Radio 4.

In 1993, Unsworth joined the BBC's Newsgathering Department, where she had responsibility for UK domestic news. She was a producer and editor for the "BBC One O'Clock News" and the "BBC Six O'Clock News." Unsworth was appointed Head of Newsgathering in January 2005.

In December 2005, Unsworth faced accusations of double standards in BBC News reporting of racial crimes when white people were the victims, on the BBC's "Newswatch" program.

Unsworth served in various senior positions in the BBC, including director of the BBC World Service Group and Acting Director of News at the BBC from November 2012 until August 2013. She was a member of the BBC's executive board and was appointed Deputy Director of News and Current Affairs in 2013. In January 2018, she was appointed Director, News & Current Affairs for BBC News, succeeding James Harding.

In August 2014, Unsworth ordered helicopter filming of a police raid on a mansion belonging to Cliff Richard, which led to the singer suing the BBC for breach of privacy. In July 2018, Sir Cliff won his case for damages.

Unsworth is a board member of the Society of Editors, the European Union's Erasmus Mundus program, and was president of the Society of Editors between 2011–12

IU has since released several successful albums, including "Modern Times" (2013), which departed from her girlish image and attempted various styles of music such as swing, jazz, and bossa nova.

IU has also acted in various television series, including "The Producers" in 2015, for which she was the new face of cosmetic brand ISOI and Unionbay Sportswear, with whom she had product placement deals. She has also collaborated with other artists, such as Gain from Brown Eyed Girls, Jonghyun from Shinee, and jazz guitarist Kim Jong-kook.

In 2017, IU released the album "Palette", which was ranked the best K-pop album of the year by Billboard and featured on the New York Times Magazine's list of "25 Songs That Tell Us Where Music Is Going". During the promotional period of "Palette", IU joined the reality program "Hyori's Homestay". IU has also released several cover albums, including "A Flower Bookmark" in 2018.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Zelma Wilson.
answer:
Zelma Wilson was an American architect who primarily practiced in California. She was born on November 23, 1918, in New York City to Russian Jewish immigrants. Raised in Santa Paula, California, by her mother Rose (a shopkeeper) and her stepfather, Ed Kraus, she graduated from Santa Paula Union High School where she played on the tennis team.

After her education, she majored in art at the University of California, Berkeley, and later studied at the California Institute of Technology. She then attended the USC School of Architecture, where she was the only woman in her class.

In 1947, Zelma Wilson graduated and began working as a draftsperson at the Los Angeles City Planning Department. In 1948, she married screenwriter Michael Wilson with whom she had two daughters. The couple was members of the American Communist Party from 1938 until early 1950s.

In 1952, her husband was blacklisted, and the family moved to France. While in Paris, Zelma pursued her interest in sculpture at the École des Beaux-Arts. She earned her architecture license in 1957, and worked with notable architects such as Richard Neutra, Victor Gruen, Rudolph Schindler, and Raphael Soriano.

The Wilson family returned to California in 1964 and settled in Ojai. Zelma Wilson opened her architectural practice in Ojai, Zelma Wilson and Associates, AIA, in 1967. She primarily designed community buildings such as schools, churches, and the Arts Theater.

Zelma Wilson's professional papers are held at Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University in Blacksburg. She was presented with her husband's posthumous Academy Award in 1985. In 1994, she received the City of Ojai's "Lifetime Achievement in the Arts Award."

Zelma Wilson died in 1996, days before she was scheduled to be an honored guest of the Ojai Film Society. There is a plaque in Libbey Park in Ojai, dedicating a nearby tree to her in recognition of her contributions as a pioneering architect, city planner, conservationist, teacher, and mentor

Following his "Idol" victory, Lummis signed a contract with music giant Sony BMG and released his debut single "They Can't Take That Away", which debuted at number one on the New Zealand Singles Chart and was certified 4xPlatinum. He then released his debut album, "One Road", which sold 45,000 copies and was certified 3xPlatinum.

After his departure from "New Zealand Idol", Lummis embarked on a nationwide tour with his fellow finalists. He then took a career break following his debut album and departure from Sony BMG, but returned in 2006 with the single "Gotta Move", which he released independently and exclusively through his personal website.

Lummis has been working on a new album since late 2007 and has also appeared on various television shows, including the TVNZ morning show, Good Morning, where he made a live performance of one of his new tracks called, "Smooth Lady", the first song from the album. Lummis is a devout Pentecostal Christian and credits his success to God, with the understanding that, however far it takes him, he will always be able to remember his time in the spotlight.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Lees Knowles.
answer:
Lees Knowles, born on February 16, 1857, was a British barrister, military historian, and Conservative politician. He was the son of John Knowles and Elizabeth Lees of Green Bank, Oldham, Lancashire, whose family owned Andrew Knowles and Sons, collieries in the Irwell Valley. He was educated at Rugby School and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he was a prominent athlete and became president of the Cambridge University Athletics Club. He studied law and was called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn in 1882.

Knowles was involved in Unionist politics and stood for election several times. He served as the Member of Parliament for Salford West from 1886 to 1906. In 1903, he was created a baronet, a title in the Baronetage of the United Kingdom.

Knowles had a great interest in military history and wrote a number of books on the life of Napoleon. In 1912, he made a bequest to his "alma mater", Trinity College, which established the Lees Knowles Lectureship, an annual series of talks on military science given by distinguished military and naval figures. He held a commission as an officer in the Volunteer Force and its successor the Territorial Force, reaching the rank of lieutenant-colonel. After a stint as Honorary Colonel of the 3rd (Volunteer) battalion of the Lancashire Fusiliers, he was appointed Honorary Colonel of the 1st (Volunteer) battalion of the King's Own Yorkshire Light Infantry.

Knowles lost his seat at the 1906 general election. He was a philanthropist, supporting a number of charities, notably the Guinness Trust for Housing the Poor. He died in October 1928, aged 71, at his home in Westwood, Pendlebury. Two roads in Llandudno, North Wales, are named in his honor: Lees Road and Knowles Road. The Knowles baronetcy became extinct on his death in 1928.

During World War II, Kyu's mother took him and his siblings to live with their maternal grandparents in rural Kasama, Ibaraki Prefecture, due to air raids over the greater Tokyo area. They moved back to Kawasaki in 1949.

In high school, Kyu started playing guitar and soon began singing. In 1958, he joined the Japanese pop-band The Drifters, but was unhappy about his position as second vocalist, which often led to fights within the band. In 1961, Sakamoto achieved success with his single "Ue o muite arukō", composed by Shinichi Nakamura. This song became one of the most popular songs in Japan and was covered by many artists.

Sakamoto's music has been featured in various media, such as the television show "Mad Men" and the anime "Futatsu no Spica". His song "Ue o muite arukō" was also featured in the alternate history series "The Man in the High Castle", set in 1963, the year the song debuted.

Roberto Clemente was a Puerto Rican professional baseball player and baseball broadcaster, born on August 17, 1965, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. He was born in the Santurce barrio. Roberto Clemente was a Hall of Fame right fielder who played his entire 18-year Major League Baseball career for the Pittsburgh Pirates. He was known for his strong arm, his batting skills, and his humanitarian work.

Clemente died in a plane crash off Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in Carolina, Puerto Rico, on December 31, 1972. He was flying with relief articles to be given to victims of the Nicaragua earthquake.

After his death, several places were named after him, including the Roberto Clemente Community Academy in Chicago, Illinois, the Roberto Clemente Coliseum in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and the Roberto Clemente State Park in the Morris Heights section of The Bronx, New York.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Emmett Skilton.
answer:
Emmett Skilton is a New Zealand-based actor, director, and producer, born on September 23, 1987, in Wellington. His professional career began in 2005 with a role in the comedy television series "Seven Periods with Mr Gormsby" as Willem Van der Muren.

During his high school years, Emmett performed in various New Zealand theatre productions, including the National Sheila Winn Shakespeare competition and youth improvisation troupe Joe Improv. He also appeared in television and film productions such as "Passion in Paradise", The Hot House, "The Investigator", and "Time Trackers".

After completing high school in 2005, Emmett toured New Zealand and Sydney with the acting company "The Ugly Shakespeare Company". He was later accepted into Wellington tertiary institute Toi Whakaari: New Zealand Drama School in 2007, where he starred in the feature film "Home By Christmas" while studying. He graduated in 2009 with a Bachelor of Performing Arts (Acting).

Emmett's most notable on-camera roles include Axl Johnson in the comedy-drama "The Almighty Johnsons", Sam Giancana in the US series "", and Victor Lownes in "". He has also co-created, directed, and produced comedy web series "Auckward Love".

In addition to his on-screen work, Emmett has performed in numerous successful theatre seasons, including "Tribes", "Paper Sky", "Stones in his Pockets", and "Between Two Waves" centering on Climate Change. He is also a screen tutor at leading drama school "The Actors Program", where he directed their 2017 and 2018 graduation films, "Ripple" and "13 Suspects". He is currently co-directing Stan Harrington's Australian based series, "Legends", due for release in 2019. Emmett has also completed a third series of his New Zealand-based series, "Best Friends", with funding from "Television New Zealand" and "NZ On Air".

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Antonio Gasalla.
answer:
Antonio Gasalla is an Argentine actor, comedian, and theatre director, born on March 9, 1941, in Ramos Mejía, a western suburb of Buenos Aires. He began his career in Buenos Aires' theatre scene in 1964 as an understudy and later became known for his work in café-concerts with Uruguayan émigré Carlos Perciavalle. Their production of "Help Valentino!" (1966) made them among the popular figures in Argentine theatre and television.

Gasalla's female impersonations have been a hallmark of his career, known for their intricate portrayals and sheer number. Some of his best-known impersonations include his role as Mamá Cora in "La carroza" (Waiting for the Hearse), where he underwent four hours of prosthetic and makeup work daily. This role introduced Gasalla to the act of female impersonation.

In 1980, Gasalla joined the cast of "El mundo de Antonio Gasalla" ("Antonio Gasalla's World"), which further cemented his popularity as a sketch comedy actor and writer. He hosted or starred in numerous variety programs on Argentine television, mostly for Channel 9, with the most popular being "El palacio de los humoristas" ("The Palace of Comedians").

In 2004, Gasalla hosted "Gasalla en pantalla" ("Gasalla on the Screen") and portrayed an irreverent elderly woman for Susana Giménez's popular variety show, earning him another Martín Fierro Prize. He has also collaborated in homages to the late comedian Niní Marshall and for the Maipo Theatre's centennial, and portrayed Argentine President Cristina Kirchner in Nito Artaza's "Cristina en el país de las maravillas" ("Cristina in Wonderland").

Recently, Gasalla directed Hernán Casciari's "Más respeto que soy tu madre" ("More Respect - I'm Your Mother"), playing the title role. Gasalla remains among the most successful and influential figures in Argentine comedy and theatre.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Rob Furlong.
answer:
Rob Furlong, born on November 11, 1976, on Fogo Island, Newfoundland, is a Canadian former military sniper who held the record for the longest confirmed sniper kill in combat at 2,430 meters (1.51 miles) until 2009. Furlong taught himself to fire a rifle ambidextrously and enlisted with the Canadian Army, serving with the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.

In March 2002, Furlong participated in Operation Anaconda in Afghanistan's Shah-i-Kot Valley. His sniper team included Master-Corporal Arron Perry, Master-Corporal Graham Ragsdale, Master-Corporal Tim McMeekin, and Corporal Dennis Eason. Furlong's team was awarded the Bronze Star Medal by the U.S. Army for their actions during Operation Anaconda.

Furlong's longest kill shot was recorded during Operation Anaconda, where he used a .50-calibre McMillan Brothers Tac-50 rifle to kill a fighter carrying an RPK machine gun at a distance of 2,430 meters. After leaving the Canadian Army, Furlong moved to Edmonton, Alberta, and joined the Edmonton Police Service in 2004. However, in 2012, Furlong was dismissed from the police for discreditable conduct.

After his dismissal from the police, Furlong operates a marksmanship academy, called Rob Furlong's Marksmanship Academy, based in Alberta.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Baltasar Corrada del Río.
answer:
Baltasar Corrada del Río was a Puerto Rican politician who was born on April 10, 1935, and passed away on March 11, 2018. He held various high political offices in Puerto Rico, including President of the Puerto Rico Civil Rights Commission, Resident Commissioner (1977–1985), Mayor of the capital city of San Juan (1985–1989), Puerto Rico's 15th Secretary of State (1993–1995), and Associate Justice of the Supreme Court (1995–2005). He was also the unsuccessful NPP candidate for Governor in the elections of 1988.

Corrada del Río obtained his high school diploma from Colegio Ponceño de Varones in 1952, and he pursued further education to earn his Bachelor's Degree. He served in various political roles, including as a keynote speaker at events alongside other notable figures such as McClintock and Chief Justice Federico Hernandez Denton.

In 2010, former Puerto Rico Secretary of State McClintock designated the department's summer internship program as the Baltasar Corrada del Río State Department Internship Program. Distinguished students such as Josue Rivera, former National President of the Puerto Rico Statehood Students Association, participated in the First Class of interns. A book containing excerpts from 61 of his Supreme Court opinions, titled Baltasar Corrada Del Río-Sus opiniones 1995-2005, was published in 2010, and a ceremony was held to announce its publication.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Nisar Ahmad Kakru.
answer:
Nisar Ahmad Kakru was born on 26 October 1949 in Baramulla, Kashmir, India. He started his legal career by practicing at the Baramulla district and sessions courts and other courts from August 1975. In 1978, he was appointed as a public prosecutor in the district and sessions court of Baramulla, a position he held until 1981 due to an order issued by the Government of Jammu and Kashmir.

Kakru was enrolled as a vakil in February 1979 and as an advocate in April 1982. He continued his private practice at Baramulla until 1984, after which he started practice at the Jammu and Kashmir High Court in 1984. He handled various types of cases including civil, criminal, constitutional, service, labor, revenue, and company matters.

In February 1988, Kakru was appointed as a Chief Government Advocate and Additional Advocate General at Jammu and Kashmir High Court by the Government of Jammu and Kashmir. He resigned from this position in 1990 due to the imposition of the Governor’s rule in the State. He continued his private practice until 1996, when he was again appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir till he was promoted to the bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir in November 1997.

During his tenure as a judge of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court, Kakru made a significant contribution to the legal field. One of his landmark judgments was during his tenure when he held that migrants from Doda and Poonch districts should be treated on par with migrants of Kashmir province.

Kakru was appointed as the Acting Chief Justice of Jammu and Kashmir High Court on several occasions from April 2007 to January 2009. Finally, on 16 February 2010, he was appointed as a Chief Justice of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh following a recommendation by the Supreme Court which was approved by the President of India. He retired upon attaining superannuation as the Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Martín Lousteau.
answer:
Martín Lousteau was born on December 8, 1970, in Buenos Aires, Argentina. He graduated from Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires. Lousteau served as the Minister of Economy and Production of Argentina under the administration of President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, from December 10, 2007, until April 24, 2008. At the age of 37, he was the youngest person to occupy this office in more than five decades.

After his tenure as the Minister of Economy and Production, Lousteau briefly served as the Argentine Ambassador to the United States from 2015 to 2017. In 2017, he ran for National Deputy in the mid-term elections, heading the Evolución Coalition, which included the Radical Civic Union and the Socialist Party. Despite coming in third with 12.3% of the vote, he and Carla Carrizo became National Deputies due to Argentina's proportional representation electoral system.

Since 2017, Lousteau has been a National Deputy, representing Buenos Aires City. It's worth noting that in 2015, Horacio Rodríguez Larreta, who was running for the mayor of Buenos Aires, narrowly defeated Lousteau in a tight two-round election.

There was a notable incident involving Lousteau and Guillermo Moreno, a prominent businessman, in August 2010. Moreno was seen at an event running his fingers across his throat, indicating Lousteau was playing a fatal game. This was in response to Lousteau's defiance against Moreno over farm export tariffs as the Minister of Economy and Production. Lousteau indeed lost his job following this incident, while Moreno has gone from strength to strength.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Roselyn Sánchez.
answer:
Roselyn Sánchez is a Puerto Rican singer/songwriter, model, actress, producer, and writer, born on April 2, 1973, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. She is the youngest of four siblings, having three older brothers. Sánchez gained public attention in Puerto Rico as a dancer and as co-host of a variety show called "Qué Vacilón". In 1993, she won the Miss Puerto Rico Petite contest, and in 1994 she won the international title of Miss American Petite, bringing her international fame.

On television, Sánchez is best known for her roles as Elena Delgado on the CBS police procedural "Without a Trace" (2005–09), and as Carmen Luna on the Lifetime comedy-drama "Devious Maids" (2013–16). In film, she has appeared in "Rush Hour 2" (2001), "Boat Trip" (2002), "The Game Plan" (2007), and "Act of Valor" (2012).

Sánchez is also an active supporter of animal rights and a member of PETA. She recently appeared nude in a PETA ad in support of anti-fur campaign efforts. She is the spokesperson of the "Fundación de Niños San Jorge", which assists sick children from poor families.

In her personal life, Sánchez is married to actor Eric Winter, with whom she co-authored the children's book, "Sebi and the Land of Cha Cha Cha", published in 2017. The book was inspired by their daughter, Sebella 'Sebi' Rose Winter.

He was also appointed Knight of the Thistle in the 2014 New Year Honours and to the Order of the Companions of Honour in 2016.

Smith served as the Chancellor of the University of Strathclyde and Chair of the British Government-backed Green Investment Bank. He is also the Chairman of the House of Lords. In 2016, he was appointed Member of the Order of the Companions of Honour (CH) for public service, particularly in Scotland.

Smith has a long-term support of the internal audit profession, and in 2010, he was awarded an Honorary Fellowship by the Chartered Institute of Internal Auditors. He was the 2015 winner of the Royal Society of Edinburgh/Adam Smith Medal for his business leadership and his outstanding contribution to public service.

Smith was a member and vice-chairman of the Museums and Galleries Commission from 1988 to 1998. question: Question: Tell me a bio of Heinrich Harrer.
answer:
Heinrich Harrer was an Austrian mountaineer, sportsman, geographer, and author, born on July 6, 1912, in Hüttenberg, Austria. He was raised in the district of Sankt Veit an der Glan in the state of Carinthia, with his father being a postal worker. Harrer studied geography and sports at the Karl-Franzens University in Graz.

In 1935, Harrer was designated to participate in the Alpine skiing competition at the 1936 Winter Olympics, but the Austrian Alpine skiing team boycotted the event due to a conflict regarding the skiing instructors' status as professionals, so Harrer did not participate. In 1937, Harrer won the downhill event at the World Student Championships at Zell am See.

Mountain climbing was Harrer's true passion. In 1938, knowing an extraordinary feat of climbing could win him a place on a Himalayan expedition, Harrer and several others attempted to climb the North Face of the Eiger in Switzerland, which they successfully achieved in 1938, becoming the first ascent of the North Face of the Eiger.

In 1939, Harrer was imprisoned in a British internment camp in India for five years due to his involvement in the Anschluss, the annexation of Austria by Nazi Germany. After his release, he was sent to a camp in Kenya. In 1944, he escaped and made his way to Lhasa, Tibet, where he lived for seven years.

During his time in Tibet, Harrer became the Dalai Lama's tutor in English, geography, and some science. A strong friendship developed between the two that would last the rest of their lives. In 1952, Harrer returned to Austria where he documented his experiences in the books "Seven Years in Tibet" (1952) and "Lost Lhasa" (1953).

In October 2002, the Dalai Lama presented Harrer with the International Campaign for Tibet's Light of Truth Award for his efforts to bring the situation in Tibet to international attention. Harrer died on January 7, 2006, in Friesach, Austria

Focus, in the context of photography and cinematography, refers to the process of adjusting the lens to bring a specific part of the image into sharp clarity while the rest of the image is blurred. This technique is known as shallow focus.

In the realm of photography, shallow focus is used to emphasize a particular subject or area of the image. The aesthetic quality of the out-of-focus area is often referred to as bokeh. The opposite of shallow focus is deep focus, where the entire image is in focus. Shallow focus has gained popularity in the 2000s and 2010s.

In the past, a focusing system called scale focus or zone focus was used in inexpensive cameras from the 1940s and 1950s. This system required the photographer to estimate the distance to the subject and set the focus using a scale printed on the lens.

In the field of language education, Focus on Form (FonF) is an approach that makes learners aware of the grammatical form of language features they can already use communicatively. It contrasts with "focus on forms" and "focus on meaning."

In precision optics, such as advanced amateur astronomical telescopes and laboratory microscopes, a device called a dual speed focuser is used. This mechanism provides two focusing speeds, one for fast focusing and another for fine focusing when the film or CCD is near the perfect focal plane.

In filmmaking and television production, a device called a follow focus is used. It is a focus control mechanism that is ergonomic rather than strictly necessary. It is used with film cameras and professional video cameras to facilitate precise focus adjustments during filming.

In 2007, Oliphant served as President of Enthought, and in 2012, he founded Continuum Analytics. Continuum Analytics is the company behind the Python distribution Anaconda, which received $24 million in Series A Funding in July 2015.

Oliphant is also a founding contributor to the SciPy packages in Python and is the primary creator of NumPy. He has received a $100,000 award from DARPA for the feasibility of designing a high-level data-parallel language extension to Python on graphics processing units (GPUs).

In addition to his professional accomplishments, Oliphant is a member of the advisory council of the non-profit scientific computing foundation NumFocus and is the author of the textbook "Guide To NumPy" and associated manuals.
